paper_metadata.title: Thalamocortical coherence predicts persistent postconcussive symptoms

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment source (TMUH), and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (GCS score, loss of consciousness duration, CT results). Baseline characteristics are well-documented in Table 1, and the sample is demographically matched to controls.

items.evidence_snippet: Patients with concussion (defined by the following criteria: closedhead injury (CHI), loss of consciousness lasting < 30 min, initial Glasgow Coma Scale score > 13, and normal head CT results) and demographically matched healthy controls (HCs) were recruited from Taipei Medical University Hospital (TMUH)
items.reasoning: The authors define the clinical criteria for concussion and the specific hospital setting.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a very high rate of attrition over the 2-year follow-up (75.7% loss). While the authors acknowledge this and compare baseline characteristics of completers vs. non-completers, the high loss to follow-up significantly increases the risk of attrition bias, as those with persistent symptoms might be more likely to remain in the study.

items.reasoning: A follow-up rate of 24.3% at 2 years is well below the standard threshold for low risk (usually >80%).
